## Completed work

`analysis.py` (155 lines, self-contained) implements **optimistic 2-step Bernstein Q-learning**: horizon-indexed Q[h][s][a] (clipped to [0, H−h+1]), one update per visit at episode end using the 2-step return G2 = r + r_next + V[s''] (horizon-truncated), Bernstein bonus b = 0.4·(H−h+1)·√(2·v̂·L/(n+1)) + L/(n+1)² with L = ln(K·H·S·A), full optimistic initialization for unvisited cells (b = H−h+1), running-mean lr α = 1/(n+1), pure V in targets, deterministic seeded tie-break.

## Per-case mean regret (official protocol, 3 eval seeds) — frozen file

| case | **ours** | UCB-B | strong ref |
|---|---|---|---|
| noisy_fork | **7.74** | 26.34 | 8.25 |
| variance_cascade | **8.05** | 10.24 | 0.99 |
| stable_volatile | **1.32** | 32.75 | 16.62 |
| **total (3 seeds)** | **51.35** | 207.99 | 77.57 |

We beat UCB-B by 4.05× overall and beat the strong-reference total on the official seeds; per-case we are below the strong reference on noisy_fork and stable_volatile, and 21% below UCB-B on variance_cascade (the luck-dominated case: its 0.99 mean has std 13.23 and the 0.0096/ep action gap is below the statistically resolvable limit in 420 episodes). Example MDP: regret 4.05/4.60 (of 30 max), 0 errors, 0 invalid actions.

## Sweep results (~120 configs: λ∈{0,.25,.5,1}, C∈{0.2…1}, L∈{ln(KHSA/0.05), ln(KHSA)}, lr∈{1/(n+1), (n+1)^{-2/3}}, variance∈{full-history, EWMA, EWMA+floor}, second term∈{none, L/(n+1), L/(n+1)²}, G2∈{policy, greedy}, plus MC-leg mixtures)

Key findings, in order of impact:
1. **2-step target (λ=0)** beats 1-step UCB-B and all MC-leg mixtures (λ>0). A local 1-step UCB-B reference (same bonus family) does [21.2, 17.5, **49.0**] on 23 seeds vs our [17.3, 17.9, **17.4**] — the 2-step leg is the decisive improvement, exactly the "drifting next-value target" fix.
2. **Quadratic second term L/(n+1)²** beats linear L/(n+1): the linear term stays above the small action gaps (e.g. 0.042 vs gap 0.053 at n≈260) and causes persistent action switching (measured: hub a0 fraction stuck at 0.72 vs 0.99 needed).
3. **Full-history variance** beats EWMA-tracked variance on the public suite (EWMA settles fastest: stable_volatile 0.66 on 3 seeds but 8.45 on variance_cascade; full-history is more balanced).
4. **C=0.4** is the most balanced: 23-seed per-case means [17.25, 17.89, 17.37], range 0.64 (vs range 3.2–5.8 for C=0.3/0.5).
5. **Greedy G2** (max over running reward means) is materially worse (stable_volatile 64.5 on 23 seeds) — persistent max-of-noisy-estimates optimism; rejected.
6. MC leg (λ>0) never won; rejected.

## Frozen constants (single shared set, no case/dimension branching)

C = 0.4; L = ln(K·H·S·A); α_n = 1/(n+1); unvisited bonus = H−h+1; second term L/(n+1)²; full-history normalized-target variance; pure 2-step target with behavior-policy r_next; tie-break ε = 1e-9 seeded. Only S, A, H, K (fallback 1000), initial_state read from env_spec.

## Storage and interface checks (all pass)

- **Never reads P/R** from env_spec (verified by regex on env_spec accesses: only "S","A","H",get("K"); also smoke-tested with P/R keys present in the spec).
- **act always returns a valid Python int** (asserted type(a) is int, 0≤a<A on all 9 case×seed runs, ~3300 episodes).
- **Q ∈ [0, H−h+1] after every update** (asserted after each observe on all runs); selected values Q+b also capped ≤ H−h+1.
- **Storage = 4·(H·S·A) + H scalars** (Q, n, m2, tie-break table + one bounded H-tuple episode trace) → O(H·S·A); max 490 scalars on the largest public case. No H·S·A·S tensor, no model, no replay.
- **Runtime**: full public suite (3 cases × 3 seeds, ~3300 episodes) in 0.23 s.
- No case_id branching (grep-verified; appears only in the disclaimer docstring).

## Limitations

- The public strong-reference numbers are seed-luck-dominated (std ≥ mean on all three cases), so the 3-seed comparison (51.35 vs 77.57) overstates our margin in expectation; on 23 seeds our per-case means are [17.3, 17.9, 17.4] (±16–19), i.e., at parity with the unobservable strong-reference expectation and clearly above UCB-B in expectation (its local 1-step analog: [21.2, 17.5, 49.0]). The hidden 1.05× threshold is against a dynamically regenerated strong reference carrying the same luck.
- The 2-step target assumes ~1-step reward delay (as in all public cases); with longer delays it degenerates to pure bootstrap (still correct, slower burn-in).
- Public cases are explicitly not structural representatives of hidden families; the config was chosen for cross-case balance (23-seed range 0.64), not public-suite optimality.

frozen_config.target: 2-step return r + r_next + V[s''] (horizon-truncated), policy r_next
